newsitem.title: UK: ICI down as analysts rejig 1997 estimates.
newsitem.headline: ICI down as analysts rejig 1997 estimates.

text.p: Shares in Imperial Chemical Industries Plc were steady near two-year lows by late morning on Thursday as some analysts cut forecasts after the company's lower-than-expected first-quarter results.
The stock was down 24p at 696-1/2 by 1039 GMT in volume of 4.4 million shares, close to its two-year low of 679p set April 4.

At Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, analysts cut their 1997 pre-tax profit estimate to 500 million stg from 590 million, dealers said, though analysts at the brokerage were not immediately available for comment.

SBC Warburg was said to be poised to trim estimates but advised clients to "buy on weakness," while other analysts said there was little positive to be gleaned from a post-results briefing with the company.

"They tried to put a positive spin on the results from the paints business but I think most went away from the meeting pretty negative," said one analyst. "There are going to be some substantial downgrades."
The consensus for 1997 pre-tax profit before today's figures was 650 million stg, according to the Estimate Directory, with forecasts ranging from 560 million to 900 million.

Earlier, ICI said paints profits had doubled in what was seasonally its weakest quarter, though analysts pointed out that recent southern-hemisphere acquisitions had changed the seasonal pattern of the unit.
Profit expectations for the group have already been sharply lowered in recent months, one reason ICI shares dropped ten percent in the first three months of the year.
ICI's pre-tax profits before exceptional items dropped to 65 million stg from 202 million a year before, compared with expectations mostly in a range between 75 million stg and 90 million.

Dealers noted that ICI was suffering a price squeeze in chemicals such as polyester and tioxide, but said the outlook for the second half was better and that 40 million stg of the profit decline was due to the strong pound.
"As soon as sterling turns round you won't see this stock for dust," one dealer said.
